title: Will provenance help games made with AI tools earn audience trust?
author: aspearin
selftext:
How will we parse the true talent from what’s emerged from the slop bucket? Same way as always: bring the creative artist forward into the spotlight.

“I quit \[lost\] my day job to make games” is a tired narrative and one we will keep seeing. There is more than that. 

Look at any other creative industry and it’s the artist with creative and financial control that at the end of the day will prevail. An artist is human. 

We need to bring forward the true creative visionaries that are shedding the shackles of external control to manifest games worth our time. 

These “one shot” remakes are only catching attention because this tech is new. What will endure are those working behind the scenes every day on some with greater purpose. It’s only a matter of time before we start seeing these projects quietly emerge. 

To be an artist is to explore identity. Bring yours forward in your work and with your work. 

Thanks for listening to my TED talk.
